title: Oracle SQL Features and Portability
learningObjectives: Recognize common Oracle SQL syntax and built-in functions.
Explain the traditional DUAL table use and modern alternatives.
Identify NVL, SYSDATE, sequences and FETCH FIRST as Oracle-specific or product-specific features.
Compare Oracle MERGE with portable insert/update workflows.
Label Oracle-only syntax and test it in the target Oracle version.

understand.concept: Oracle Database provides SQL with Oracle-specific functions, sequence objects, data types and procedural extensions. Some syntax is standard in modern versions while other features remain vendor-specific.
understand.whyItMatters: Oracle applications often rely on sequences, NVL, date functions and MERGE. These constructs need deliberate translation when moving to another DBMS.
understand.analogy: A professional toolkit includes specialized attachments designed for one machine model.
understand.analogyLimit: Oracle version, compatibility settings and data types affect syntax and behaviour; a similar feature in another DBMS may not be semantically identical.

explain.narrative:
## Oracle-specific features
Oracle applications commonly use sequences for generated identifiers, `NVL()` for a two-argument NULL fallback, `SYSDATE` for the database server date/time and `DUAL` for selecting an expression without a user table. Modern Oracle versions support row limiting with `FETCH FIRST`.

## MERGE and procedural code
Oracle supports MERGE for conditional insert/update logic and PL/SQL for stored program units. MERGE semantics and concurrency edge cases differ among DBMS products, so test the exact workflow.

## Portable alternatives
COALESCE is broadly standardized; CASE is portable conditional logic; explicit table queries avoid depending on DUAL when the target engine permits SELECT expressions without FROM. Identity columns and sequences need engine-specific migration planning.

## Runnable examples
The examples use SQLite-compatible core SQL. Oracle-only syntax is shown as labelled reference material and is not executed by the SQLite Playground.

examples.title: Create a portable inventory table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE dialect23_inventory (item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item_name TEXT NOT NULL, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity >= 0));
examples.explanation: Creates a simple inventory relation. Oracle may use NUMBER and an identity column or sequence-backed key depending on the schema design.

examples.title: Insert inventory rows
examples.explanation: Adds two inventory rows. In Oracle, generated keys may use identity columns or sequences, and INSERT syntax should be adapted accordingly.

examples.title: Use COALESCE for a missing label
examples.code: SELECT item_name, COALESCE(CAST(quantity AS TEXT), 'Unknown') AS quantity_label FROM dialect23_inventory ORDER BY item_id;
examples.explanation: Shows a broadly supported NULL fallback. Oracle's NVL is a common vendor-specific alternative, but implicit conversion and result type should be checked.

examples.title: Calculate a portable conditional stock label
examples.code: SELECT item_name, CASE WHEN quantity = 0 THEN 'Out of stock' WHEN quantity < 10 THEN 'Low stock' ELSE 'Available' END AS stock_state FROM dialect23_inventory ORDER BY item_id;
examples.explanation: Uses searched CASE, a portable conditional expression. Oracle supports CASE as well as procedural IF statements inside PL/SQL blocks.

examples.title: Aggregate inventory quantities
examples.code: SELECT COUNT(*) AS item_count, SUM(quantity) AS total_units FROM dialect23_inventory;
examples.explanation: Uses standard aggregate functions. Oracle and SQLite both support COUNT and SUM, though numeric result types can differ.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and compare COALESCE with Oracle NVL in the narrative. Explain why a sequence-backed identifier is not automatically interchangeable with SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY.
practise.independentTask: Prepare an Oracle-specific reference example using a sequence, SYSDATE and FETCH FIRST. For each feature, document the closest PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite alternative and any semantic difference.
hints: Oracle has sequences and identity columns.
NVL is an Oracle-specific NULL function; COALESCE is widely supported.
SYSDATE returns the database server date/time.
DUAL is traditionally used for expression-only SELECT statements.
Test MERGE and sequence behaviour on the target Oracle version.

questions.prompt: Which function is commonly used by Oracle for a NULL fallback?
questions.explanation: NVL is a common Oracle-specific function.
SYSDATE returns the database server date/time.

questions.prompt: What is DUAL traditionally used for?
options: Selecting an expression without querying a user table
questions.answer: Selecting an expression without querying a user table
questions.explanation: DUAL is a one-row special table used for expression-only queries.

questions.prompt: Which feature generates identifiers in Oracle schemas?
questions.explanation: Oracle sequences are commonly used to generate unique values.

questions.prompt: Why should Oracle MERGE be tested on the target version?
options: Its syntax and concurrency behaviour are product-specific
questions.answer: Its syntax and concurrency behaviour are product-specific
questions.explanation: MERGE semantics and edge cases differ between database engines.
